Sara — thanks for the sample and the clear ask. Quick summary below; attaching a short PDF with the model shortlist rationale and an XLSX with token estimates for the 90-day pilot.

TL;DR recommendations (pilot / production):
- Pilot shortlist (fast iteration): Redwood-7B-Chat-quant (4k window, best latency/cost balance), Falcon-40B-instruct (16k window, for edge cases that need longer context), and Llama2-13B-8bit (8k window, sensitivity test).
- Context guidance: start pilot using a 4k prefix window for the majority of RAG summaries; route longer conversations (>4k tokens) to Falcon-40B-instruct as a fallback. This keeps average latency predictable while letting you evaluate quality trade-offs on long threads.
- Caching/KV notes: with a 4k configured prefix, typical KV cache hit rate estimated at 18–25% given your 200-sample mix. We expect caching to reduce repeat-token compute by ~12% in steady state for FAQ-like interactions.
- Hourly token profile (conservative): pilot baseline 18k tokens/hour (off-peak 6k, peak 45k) — see attached workbook for hour-by-hour bands and 90-day projection.

Requests:
1) Can you confirm expected concurrency (avg requests/sec) for the first 2 weeks of the pilot? The token-based numbers scale linearly with qps + average response length.
2) Any hard data residency or private deployment requirements for pilot?

Next steps: Connor will follow up with a short ops checklist; Monica will schedule the kickoff.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai

Hi all — a few ops-focused clarifications from my side so the Acme infra team can size properly:

- KV cache sizing: assuming average prefix ~1.2k tokens, we recommend reserving 8–16GB of GPU-side KV per concurrent model shard for the 4k window profile. If you route to Falcon-40B for long-context requests, plan an additional 12–24GB per shard during those peak minutes.
- Batching assumptions: the hourly token profile in Ava's workbook assumes 20–35% opportunistic batching during peak (mix of sync and async requests). If your frontend sends single-shot sync calls with no batching, multiply token compute by ~1.4x.
- Fallback routing: we suggest policy: 1) try Redwood-7B-Chat; 2) if response quality below threshold or context >4k, route to Llama2-13B-8bit; 3) if still low confidence, escalate to Falcon-40B-instruct. We'll instrument deterministic fallback metrics so you can measure cost vs. quality.

I've added a short checklist at the bottom of the attached ops doc: network whitelists, KMS thumbprint for private pilot, sample load tests (k6 scripts), and a stub GPU sizing table you can drop into procurement docs.

-Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
